source_question: Whether an event-wide controllability label is adequate when cancellation control and effect observations can be delayed across one operation's irreversible dispatch frontier.
allocation_delta_from_a01: A01's candidate applied the cancellation-prevented plant before branching over policies. A02 evaluates each policy's cancellation action first, derives that policy's actual plant outcome independently, and only then computes that policy's report/retry decision. A01 bytes and FAIL_HARNESS disposition remain untouched.

timing_contract.phase_index: Index into phase_order; EMITTED occurs at index 3.
timing_contract.removal_confirmed_before_emit: True only when the removal receipt arrives before EMITTED, or exactly at EMITTED with CONTROL_FIRST. A delivered cancel command alone is never removal proof.
timing_contract.effect_commit: The operation commits when EMITTED is reached unless operation removal was confirmed before that frontier.
timing_contract.retry_decision: At transition time 4.75. EFFECT_FIRST gives a committed operation's exact effect receipt at 4.1, before the retry decision. RELEASE_FIRST gives only release acknowledgement at 4.5 before the decision; a committed effect receipt arrives at 5.0 afterward. A cancel command delivered after 4.75 is unavailable to the current decision.
timing_contract.stale_receipt: STALE_EFFECT_ACK(op0) is a separate operation identity and is never accepted as evidence about op1.

policies.STATIC_CANCELABLE: Issues cancel for every phase and treats cancel-command delivery as proof of removal if no effect receipt has arrived. This intentionally optimistic static-label comparator can be false-safe.
policies.STATIC_UNCONTROLLABLE: Never issues cancel; keeps the operation pending and suppresses retry. A safe pre-emission cancellation opportunity is counted as missed only when retry was requested.
policies.PHASE_REFINED: Issues cancel only before EMITTED and admits retry only after operation-bound removal confirmation before EMITTED. Otherwise it reports COMMITTED if an effect receipt arrived, UNKNOWN if not, and suppresses retry.
policies.FAIL_CLOSED: Never issues cancel; reports UNKNOWN without an effect receipt and suppresses retry. This is a fail-closed baseline.

input_semantics: Every non-NONE row is a cancellation intent arriving at request_phase. Each policy decides whether to issue a cancel command. retry_requested independently indicates whether a second operation is waiting on the decision.
limitations: Authored deterministic finite plant only; no actual OS, GUI backend, application, model, latency, task effect, or product behavior was measured.
The static policies are explicit comparators, not a claim that every event-level supervisor uses these policies.
The phase-refined policy is given the modeled phase and bounded delay values. Real phase observability and delay bounds are unverified.
